package_info.why_malicious: The report discusses a large-scale, ongoing campaign of malicious packages published to npm (and PyPI) as part of dependency confusion attacks. These packages are considered malicious because they are intentionally crafted to exploit naming conflicts between public and private/internal repositories, allowing attackers to inject arbitrary or harmful code into build environments. The maliciousness is determined by automated detection of suspicious signals (e.g., author history, code patterns) and confirmed by manual review.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or install-time (depending on package type)
execution_context.file_location: index.js or main entrypoint of the npm package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Exfiltrates environment variables or secrets from the build environment to an external server controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code attempts to access sensitive environment variables and transmit them over the network to an untrusted external domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not exfiltrate secrets or make unsolicited network requests during install or import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or error reporting libraries may send limited, non-sensitive data to trusted endpoints, but not secrets.
key_indicators: Access to process.env or similar environment variable APIs
Network requests to non-standard or external domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious package to the public npm registry with a name matching an internal/private dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious package is pulled into the build environment due to dependency confusion.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in the package executes during install or import, harvesting secrets or performing other malicious actions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data or compromise of the build environment.

behavioral_signatures: npm package with install/import-time code that accesses environment variables
Network requests to external or suspicious domains during install/import
Package name matches known internal/private dependencies (dependency confusion pattern)
file_indicators: Presence of install scripts (preinstall, postinstall) in package.json
Code accessing process.env or similar APIs in entrypoint files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to non-standard domains during package installation
Domains not associated with legitimate telemetry or update services
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that execute code on install/import, especially those making network requests or accessing environment variables. Cross-reference package names with internal/private dependencies to identify potential dependency confusion. Use automated tools to quarantine suspicious packages and require manual review before allowing them into production environments.
